title: Shift Distance Between Two Strings
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
signature: long shiftDistance(String s, String t, int[] nextCost, int[] previousCost)
notes:
## Intuition

Each position of `s` changes on its own, so the answer adds up one trip around the alphabet circle per index. No step costs less than zero, so turning back or running a full lap never helps: the cheapest trip is either the forward arc or the backward arc. Summing an arc step by step takes up to 25 additions; prefix sums over two laps of the alphabet give it in one subtraction, even when it wraps past `'z'`.

## Approach

1. Build `nextSum` and `prevSum`: running totals of `nextCost` and `previousCost` over two laps of the alphabet.
2. For each index, read the letter numbers `from` (in `s`) and `to` (in `t`).
3. Forward pays `nextCost` for the letters `from`, `from + 1`, ..., `to - 1`. If `to` is behind `from`, it is reached on the second lap, at `to + 26`.
4. Backward pays `previousCost` for the letters `from`, `from - 1`, ..., `to + 1`. If `from` is before `to`, lift `from` to the second lap first.
5. Add the cheaper arc to `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nextCost` starts `[100, 0, ...]` and `previousCost` starts `[1, 100, 0, ...]`, so `nextSum` holds 100 at slots 1 to 26 (200 from slot 27), and `prevSum` holds 1 at slot 1, 101 at slots 2 to 26 and 102 at slot 27.

- Index 0, `'a'` to `'b'` (`from = 0`, `to = 1`): `forward = nextSum[1] - nextSum[0] = 100`; `backwardStart = 26`, so `backward = prevSum[27] - prevSum[2] = 1`. Add 1.
- Index 1, `'b'` to `'a'`: `forwardEnd = 26`, so `forward = nextSum[26] - nextSum[1] = 0`; `backward = prevSum[2] - prevSum[1] = 100`. Add 0.
- Indexes 2 and 3 repeat this, so `total = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): the prefix sums take 52 steps, then each index costs O(1).
- Space: O(1): two arrays of 53 numbers, whatever the input length.

## Pitfalls

- Backward steps are charged by the letter you leave: going from `from` down to `to` uses `previousCost[to + 1]` through `previousCost[from]`, never `previousCost[to]`.
- Forgetting the wrap: when `to < from`, the forward arc ends at `to + 26`, which is why the arrays cover two laps.
- The total can reach about 1.3 · 10^15 (up to 13 steps of 10^9 per position), beyond 32 bits: Java and C need a 64-bit sum.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nextSum`, `prevSum` | prefix sums of `nextCost` and `previousCost` over two laps (slot `k` holds the first `k` costs) |
| `from`, `to` | letter numbers of `s[i]` and `t[i]` |
| `forwardEnd` | where the forward arc ends (`to`, or `to + 26` after a wrap) |
| `backwardStart` | where the backward arc starts (`from`, or `from + 26` before a wrap) |
| `forward`, `backward` | cost of each arc for this index |
| `total` | sum of the cheaper arcs so far |

narration.2: Running totals of nextCost: slot k holds the cost of the first k forward steps from 'a'.
narration.3: The same running totals for previousCost.
narration.4: Fill two laps of the alphabet (52 steps) so an arc that wraps past 'z' is still one plain range.
narration.5: Each forward slot adds the cost of leaving letter i % 26 forward.
narration.6: Each backward slot adds the cost of leaving letter i % 26 backward.
narration.9: total collects the cheapest trip of every position.
narration.10: Positions change independently, so handle them one at a time.
narration.11: Letter number of the character s holds here.
narration.12: Letter number it has to become.
narration.13: If the target is behind the start, the forward arc wraps and ends on the second lap.
narration.14: Forward cost: nextCost of every letter from 'from' up to just before the end.
narration.15: If the start is before the target, the backward arc wraps, so lift the start to the second lap.
narration.16: Backward cost: previousCost of every letter from the start down to just above 'to'.
narration.17: Turning around never pays off, so the cheaper arc is this position's cost.
narration.19: Every position has been paid for; return the sum.
